Decision 0097: no starting bloc. Context, not an army leg. Moore's Rebellion Record vol 1 Diary of Events, Jan 1861 entry (quoting the Tribune): "CAPTAIN CHARLES STONE, upon the recommendation of General Scott, is appointed to organize the militia of the District of Columbia". This shows a District militia post under Scott's patronage (the pack's state_col 1861-01-01), not service as an officer of the US Army, so 'army' is not supported. No leg found for any other bloc.

Decision 0097: no starting bloc. No pre-start Confederate leg. His first Confederate commission in the pack is pacs_brig_gen 1861-11-02. Searched JCCS vol 1 and OR I-1 by name: no pre-start document.

Decision 0097: no starting bloc. No qualifying leg. Rebellion Record vol 1 diary 29 Dec 1860: 'J. B. Floyd, of Virginia, Secretary of War of the United States, resigns. Large frauds reported in his Department'. That is a resignation from a US cabinet post, not membership of the secession side, and he held no Confederate office or commission before 5 Mar (pack: pacs_brig_gen 1861-05-23). Propose HOLD.

Decision 0097: no starting bloc. No qualifying leg. He sat in the US Senate through the 1860-61 session (Congressional Globe daily issues of 11 Jan and 4-5 Feb 1861 show him speaking as a senator) and Virginia left only on 17 Apr. He held no Confederate post before 5 Mar. Propose HOLD.

No contemporary leg found. Chicago proceedings only show Banks as a vice-presidential candidate whose name Massachusetts withdrew for Hamlin ("The State of Massachusetts withdraws the name of Nathaniel P. Banks, and casts her vote for Mr. Hamlin"). He left the governorship in January 1861 and sat in neither house. Searched Globe 36-2 roll calls Dec 1860 to 4 Mar 1861, Chicago and the Democratic proceedings, Rebellion Record vol 1. His valedictory address of January 1861 was not found on archive.org.

No contemporary leg found. The Chicago ballot gives him 48 votes for the nomination ("For Edward Bates, of Missouri, 48") which shows his supporters but not a wing. No speech, vote or letter of his dated before 5 March 1861 was found in the Globe, Rebellion Record vol 1, the Peace Conference report or Chicago proceedings.

The only leg that separates the wings contradicts the pack: he voted nay on the House passage of the amendment against interfering with slavery in the States ("NAYS--Messrs. Alley, Ashley, Beale, Bingham, Blair, Blake") alongside Gooch, Stevens and Washburne. His other votes (yea on the repeal-of-personal-liberty-laws resolution of 17 Dec, yea on the Anderson resolution of 9 Jan) were shared by nearly all Republicans. One differentiating vote only, so HOLD and re-test.

No contemporary leg found. Chicago proceedings show him as a Maryland delegate on the credentials committee ("Mr. M. Blair, of Maryland: The Committee on Credentials") and no speech or vote of his on the winter compromise was found. He was nominated Postmaster General on 4 March 1861 (office after the leg date).

No pre-start leg for war_democrats. The 1860 proceedings show him a Democratic delegate: he offered the minority platform report at Charleston ("hereby declare our affirmance of the Democratic resolutions unanimously adopted ... at Cincinnati, in the year 1856, without addition or alteration") and at Baltimore he presented the protest of the majority of the Massachusetts delegation which withdrew ("a majority of the delegates from Massachusetts do not purpose further to participate in the doings of this Convention"). That shows a Democrat of the seceding wing, not a war Democrat. Rebellion Record vol 1 mentions him only from April 1861.

Mixed. On 19 Jan he moved to reconsider the vote adopting the Clark substitute for Crittenden's resolutions, then said: "My motion was made to accommodate the Senator from Kentucky, but I shall vote with my friends on this side." and he voted nay with the Republicans. He is not recorded on the Corwin vote or the adjournment vote of 2 March. Nothing places him in either wing.

No contemporary primary found. The only text found is Appletons' Annual Cyclopaedia 1861 summarising the inaugural of 15 Jan 1861 (he pledged to stand between the Constitution and encroachments from "hatred, ambition, fanaticism, or folly" and "The people mean to preserve the Union at every hazard") which is a reference summary and not a leg. The inaugural text itself was not found on archive.org.

His speech printed as a pamphlet is dated 7 March (after the boundary).
